observation.visible_scene: A sunset over a calm sea or large lake, viewed from a pebble beach. A transparent crystal ball (lensball) rests on wet, rounded pebbles in the left foreground, showing an inverted image of the horizon and sky inside it. The sun sits low on the horizon to the right, throwing a bright, vertical glittering reflection column across the open water. A thin distant landmass forms the horizon line under an orange-pink, lightly clouded sky.
visible_changes: The crystal ball stays fixed in the same position and size relative to the frame throughout the excerpt; the horizon line and ball position do not shift, indicating the camera is stationary.

Gentle water motion at the shoreline: small ripples and a thin wash of water advance and recede across the wet pebbles in the foreground and to the right of the ball, with the moving waterline and ripple crests visible at different positions in different frames (e.g. a ripple front crossing the right-side pebbles in mid-frames, a broader shallow sheet of water over the pebbles in later frames).

The sun's reflection column on the open water shimmers and changes shape slightly frame to frame as the surface ripples, but the sun itself and the bright spot refracted inside the ball remain essentially in place.
The inverted scene captured within the ball shifts subtly in brightness/contrast as the water and light at the shore change, but no new object appears in or around the ball.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the shoreline water is on a rising tide or merely oscillating with small waves cannot be determined from this short segment.
The full duration and any larger motion of the water, sun, or camera outside these crop boundaries are unseen.
uncertain_details: The net direction of the waterline movement (advance vs. retreat) is small and ambiguous; individual ripples move but no clear overall translation of the water edge is firmly established.
Any very slight camera drift is not distinguishable from the static background.
The exact material of the ball and the precise cause of the ripples (wind vs. wave) are not observable.
